# Capgemini Interview Experience | Exceller 2023-2024

Last Updated : 4 Sep, 2024

Hi everyone , I am 2024 CSE passout i have applied for Capgemini company as a fresher via superset platform for Software Engineer (Capgemini Exceller 2023-2024 ) . I want to share my experience of this journey of tests and interviews and I hope it helps you in your preparations .

****ROUND 1 -****

1) ****Technical Test**** - It was a MCQ test

Questions - 40 Ques

Time - 40 mins

The questions were easy to medium type. These consists of Pseudocodes , Computer Networks basic concepts, Cloud , Data Structures , Algorithms, Fundamentals of database

****Note**** - For technical test preparation , I will suggest just go through previous 3-5 year questions , most of questions pattern was same . PseudoCode Questions of previous years were really helpful in my case

2) ****English Test**** - It has duration of 30 minutes and 30 Questions . The level was easy to medium

3) ****Gaming Test**** - It consists of Games .You randomly get assigned any 4 games to play . Thing is you need to attempt and answer as many questions as you can . If you feel you can skip any particular question and move to next question

Note - For gaming , You can use google and Youtube to find tricks and strategies to solve question (It is also virtual ). In starting it might feel new and tough but after solving few questions it becomes little easy . Most important thing is time , so try to solve as many question possible and also skip question if you feel question is hard

****ROUND 2 -****

SVAR - Englis Communication Test

****FINAL ROUND 3 - INTERVIEW (Technical + HR Interview)****

Questions -

- Introduce yourself

- Projects

- Internship (she asked me to explain my schedule during internship , she asked me in detail about my projects and my role )

- Difference between Normal project in College and Internship project

- Coding related question (Basic questions difference between = and == , Prime number code )

- Ready to relocate (I answered it in positive way saying I like travelling too)

All the best !!!!

# Capgemini Interview Experience (Off-Campus) 2022

Last Updated : 20 May, 2024

I appeared for Capgemini Off-Campus Recruitment in May 2022. I asked my seniors about the preparation and Capgemini’s interview process, and they suggested I study at GFG.

Here I want to share my interview and test process which I faced for selecting the Capgemini.

#### Actually selection process of Capgemini had three rounds:

* Written Test
* Technical/HR Interview

The pattern of the test was as follows:-

### ****Quants:****

1. The time limit to attend this section was 25 minutes and it had 16 numbers.
2. This section included questions on Data Interpretation, speed and distance, algebra, equations, progression, profit and loss, ratio and percentage, averages, geometry, probability, etc.

### ****Logical Reasoning:****

1. The time limit to attend this section was 25 minutes, and it had 16 questions.
2. This section included questions on topics like visual reasoning, blood relations, flowcharts, statements and conclusions, etc.

### ****Pseudo Code:****

1. This section contained 20 questions on C, C++, OOPS concepts, Data Structures and Algorithms.
2. The time limit for this section was 30 minutes.

### ****Essay Writing:****

1. It had only one question on current affairs.
2. The time limit was 10 minutes.
3. The sectional and overall cut-off for the Capgemini written test was 70 percentile, I cleared the cut-off and therefore was eligible for the subsequent rounds.

****Round – 1: Online Test****

The initial step involved creating a new account in Superset and applying through the platform (as per college instructions, no separate registration was provided). Subsequently, login credentials for Capgemini's AON platform were sent for the test. The test comprised three sections:

****Sections Topics****

****Section – 1****

This section encompassed English MCQs alongside Technical MCQs. English MCQs primarily focused on synonyms, antonyms, voice changes, speeches, and comprehension, among others. A total of 30 questions were posed in this section.

The technical MCQ section featured questions on Python, SQL, Shell Scripting, and other technical domains. Additionally, there were pseudo codes where candidates were required to determine the output. A total of 45 questions were presented in this section.

This was also an elimination round.

****Section – 2****

Candidates who successfully cleared the English and Technical MCQ round proceeded to section 2. This was a Game-based Aptitude Round, where each candidate was randomly assigned four out of a variety of 24 games. Unlike traditional math aptitude questions, some games did not have a single correct answer. Instead, each answer carried a different point value, with the most suitable option garnering the highest points.

This was also an elimination round.

****Section – 3 (Optional)****

This round was exclusively for high-performing candidates from the previous two rounds, eligible for an enhanced package. It comprised coding questions (not MCQs) alongside a spoken English assessment. Performance in this round determined whether candidates would proceed to an interview for the higher package of 5.75 or 7.5 LPA.

THIS WAS NOT AN ELIMINATION ROUND

****Round – 2: Interviews****

Technical Interview

Interviews were scheduled based on candidates' performance in the previous rounds. As a fresher hired for the Software Engineer role, my interview lasted 30 minutes and was conducted online. The questions posed during the interview included:

* Introduce yourself briefly.

* Which programming language do you prefer among Python, SQL, and Shell Scripting? (I opted for Python)
* Distinguish between List and Tuple.
* Explain Decorator and Generator.
* Define Encapsulation.
* Explain the logic behind two code snippets: Factorial and Leap Year.
